note.explanation: Mitosis has one division and makes two daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent. Meiosis has two divisions and makes four daughter cells with half the parent cell’s chromosome number. Crossing-over occurs in meiosis and helps produce variation.
examples: If a parent cell has 8 chromosomes, mitosis produces daughter cells with 8 chromosomes each.
If a parent cell has 8 chromosomes, meiosis produces daughter cells with 4 chromosomes each.
note.checkAnswer: Meiosis has two divisions; it separates sister chromatids during anaphase II.
note.simple: Mitosis makes two similar cells. Meiosis makes four cells with half the chromosome number, and crossing-over can make them varied.
note.checkQuestion: How many divisions occur in meiosis, and when do sister chromatids separate?
note.title: Comparing Mitosis and Meiosis
steps: Check how many divisions take place: one in mitosis and two in meiosis.
Compare the number of daughter cells: two in mitosis and four in meiosis.
Compare chromosome numbers: unchanged in mitosis and reduced by half in meiosis.
Look for crossing-over: it occurs in meiosis, not mitosis.
Remember that sister chromatids separate in mitosis and in anaphase II of meiosis.
note.answer: Mitosis produces two daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent cell. Meiosis produces four daughter cells with half the chromosome number.

written.text: How does crossing over contribute to genetic variation in meiosis?
written.finalAnswer: Crossing-over exchanges segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, producing variations.

written.text: What is the difference between prophase of mitosis and prophase-I of meiosis-I?
written.finalAnswer: In prophase of mitosis, chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes and homologous chromosomes do not form pairs or cross over. In prophase-I of meiosis-I, homologous chromosomes form pairs and non-sister chromatids exchange segments in crossing-over.

written.text: Describe the events that occur during the phases of meiosis-I.
written.finalAnswer: During prophase I, homologous chromosomes form pairs and non-sister chromatids exchange segments in crossing-over. During metaphase I, pairs of homologous chromosomes attach to spindle fibres from opposite poles and align. During anaphase I, homologous chromosomes are pulled apart to opposite poles. During telophase I, spindle fibres disappear and a new nuclear envelope surrounds each haploid set.

examTips: A short question may ask you to compare chromosome number, daughter-cell number, cell type, or crossing-over in mitosis and meiosis.
For a comparison, write both sides clearly: for example, “same as the parent” for mitosis and “reduced by half” for meiosis.
For a question about meiosis-I phases, use the order prophase I, metaphase I, anaphase I, telophase I and state the event in each phase.
Marks are often awarded for the correct event and its phase; do not name an event without naming the phase.
For significance of meiosis, include haploid gametes, maintenance of chromosome number, and variation.

example.question: Compare mitosis and meiosis in terms of number of divisions, daughter cells, chromosome number, and crossing-over.
example.answer: Mitosis has one division and produces two daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent; it does not involve crossing-over. Meiosis has two divisions and produces four daughter cells with half the chromosome number; crossing-over occurs and variations are produced.

explain.title: What the two divisions share
explain.body: DNA replication occurs during interphase (S phase) before both divisions. Both divisions also involve chromosome condensation, spindle formation, and the stages prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase. Cytokinesis occurs at the end of both divisions.

explain.title: How many cells are made
explain.body: In mitosis, a parent cell divides once and produces two daughter cells. In meiosis, a parent cell undergoes two divisions and produces four daughter cells.

explain.title: How chromosome number changes
explain.body: In mitosis, the chromosome number in daughter cells remains the same as the parent cell. In meiosis, the chromosome number is reduced by half in daughter cells.

explain.title: Pairing and crossing-over
explain.body: In mitosis, homologous chromosomes do not form pairs and crossing-over does not occur. In meiosis, homologous chromosomes form pairs and crossing-over occurs during prophase. This helps produce variations.

explain.title: Where and why they occur
explain.body: Mitosis occurs in somatic cells and supports growth, development, and maintenance. Meiosis occurs in germ line cells and produces gametes in animals and spores in plants for sexual reproduction.

explain.title: When sister chromatids separate
explain.body: Sister chromatids separate during anaphase in mitosis. In meiosis, they separate during anaphase II; homologous chromosomes separate during anaphase I.

mistakes: Do not say meiosis produces two daughter cells; it produces four.
Do not say the chromosome number stays the same in meiosis; it is reduced by half.
Do not confuse homologous chromosomes separating in anaphase I with sister chromatids separating in anaphase II.
Do not say crossing-over occurs in mitosis; it occurs in prophase of meiosis.
When describing metaphase, distinguish a single chromosome aligning in mitosis from homologous pairs aligning in meiosis.
Do not forget to state the phase when naming an event in a question about meiosis-I.
